newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault 1996 truck sales down 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Renault 1996 truck sales down 16 pct.

text.p: Renault V.I., the commercial vehicle arm of Renault, said sales fell 16 percent last year to 63,680 units, reflecting weakness in demand and the impact of the renewal of some models.
Renault, which owns U.S. Mack Trucks, said market conditions would be difficult next year in both Europe and the United States.
"In Europe, a declining trend is anticipated in 1997," it said in a statement. "In the United States, the market should continue a contraction to reach its average level in 1997."

Renault V.I. said its share of the shrinking European market for trucks over five tonnes was 11 percent in 1996, down from 11.2 percent in the previous year. Its share of the stagnant European market for trucks over 16 tonnes was unchanged at 11.8 percent in 1996.
In the United States, where the market shrank 15 percent from peak 1995 levels, Mack Trucks had 12.1 percent of the Class 8 segment, up from 12 percent in 1995.
Renault said group sales of trucks between five and 16 tonnes fell last year to 59,250 units from 69,930 in 1995. In the higher category, unit sales fell to 45,600 from 53,900.

Renault said its 1996 sales were affected by the replacement of the Manager and Major lines by the new Premium line, but it said the new line had been well received. More than 7,000 models were delivered in 1996, in line with company objectives.
